tasks.short: Discuss illnesses and treatments with patients and families

steps.what: Review the current illness and treatment information and clarify what may be discussed
outputs: verified discussion scope and open clinical questions

steps.what: Discuss illnesses and treatments with patients and family members and check their understanding
inputs: verified discussion scope and open clinical questions

tasks.design: Retain the nurse's discussion with patients and families using current clinical information {OTHER}. No generated advice or automatic family message replaces clarification, empathy or understanding checks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Information must be appropriate to this patient and understandable in an emotionally demanding situation.
tasks.enabler_now: Current records support the conversation; documentation tools do not establish a shorter discussion.
tasks.still_hard: Explain uncertainty and respond to conflicting questions or misunderstandings.
tasks.human_edge: Notice emotional and comprehension needs and adapt the explanation.

reach.task: Resolve questions beyond the nurse's information or authority
reach.learn: Which uncertainties need a shared explanation

evidence.claim: A clinical documentation capability does not demonstrate reduced patient and family discussion time.

assumptions: Care staff produce the existing care record during treatment; the nurse verifies current scope and sharing preferences in s1.
The nurse elicits questions and checks understanding in s2; all elicitation and communication remain counted.
No free structured family permission flag or new patient-information feed is assumed; ambiguity is resolved in retained time.
Patient and family time remains unchanged outside focal savings; no new system or upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Current information-sharing practices and common questions
research_questions: Which illness or treatment uncertainties most often require clinician clarification?

already_counted.description: Scope verification and discussion remain fully counted.

incremental.description: No new patient communication service or upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and zero incremental work give zero saving. Conversation and understanding checks retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Diagnose conditions associated with rapid deterioration

steps.what: Examine patient findings and review symptoms, history and available diagnostic evidence for deterioration
outputs: verified findings and unresolved clinical evidence

steps.what: Diagnose acute or chronic conditions within scope and communicate instability concerns for further clinical action
inputs: verified findings and unresolved clinical evidence
outputs: documented clinical assessment and communicated instability concerns

tasks.design: Retain nurse-led assessment and diagnostic reasoning within verified professional scope, using current clinical records {OTHER}. No general diagnostic model or automatic deterioration classification is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Deterioration risk requires contextual interpretation of incomplete, changing evidence.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing diagnostic information supports the work; specialised imaging evidence does not establish this broad capability.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguish competing explanations and recognise uncertainty that demands further review.
tasks.human_edge: Integrate the patient's presentation with evidence and communicate concern responsibly.
tasks.altitude: Accountable clinical assessment remains the task.

reach.task: Review instability concerns beyond nursing diagnostic scope
reach.learn: Which findings and uncertainties require further evaluation

evidence.claim: Transpara supports mammography interpretation, which does not establish general acute care deterioration diagnosis automation.

assumptions: The worker's actual diagnostic authority is verified; where independent diagnosis is outside scope, the output is a nursing assessment and escalated concern.
The nurse produces and verifies current findings in s1 and captures assessment and communication in s2; all acquisition, reasoning and capture time remains.
Diagnostic staff produce available results in existing testing processes; no free reconciled evidence or new risk score is assumed.
This scope overlaps urgent condition assessment and must not receive additive savings; no new system upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Local authority, care setting and current diagnostic support
research_questions: Which evidence gaps commonly require additional clinician review?

already_counted.description: Finding verification and clinical reasoning remain fully counted.

incremental.description: No new diagnostic system or maintenance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and zero incremental work yield zero saving. No reduction in assessment, diagnosis or clinical communication is supported.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assess urgent and emergent conditions using clinical and technological data

steps.what: Gather and verify physiological observations and technologically derived data for the current patient
outputs: verified current observations and device context

steps.what: Assess urgent and emergent health conditions and communicate care needs and uncertainty
inputs: verified current observations and device context
outputs: documented urgent assessment and communicated care needs

tasks.design: Keep urgent assessment with the nurse using existing monitoring devices and clinical records {OTHER}. No new integrated sensor stream, autonomous triage or generated urgency judgement is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings can be stale, unreliable or inconsistent with the patient and require clinical interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing devices provide data already used in the baseline.
tasks.still_hard: Determine which observations are reliable and what they mean together in the current situation.
tasks.human_edge: Relate readings to the actual patient and communicate uncertainty promptly.

reach.task: Clarify concerns raised by urgent assessment
reach.learn: Which observation context matters during handoff

evidence.claim: Access to technological readings does not establish reduced clinical assessment work in this unchanged design.

assumptions: The nurse acquires current physiological observations and verifies patient, timing and device context in s1; all acquisition time remains.
Existing devices produce readings through current operation, and prior care staff produce the history; no newly cleaned integrated feed is assumed.
Assessment, recording and communication remain in s2; no free structured urgency flag is introduced.
This task overlaps deterioration diagnosis and is not an additive opportunity; no new equipment or upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Current monitoring setup and data reliability issues
research_questions: Which device or timing ambiguities require repeat verification during urgent assessment?

already_counted.description: Observation verification and urgent assessment remain fully counted.

incremental.description: No new sensor integration or maintenance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and no incremental work yield zero saving. Current device assistance is already in the baseline.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Document assessment, interventions, medication and patient responses

steps.what: Identify the patient encounter and verify source assessment, intervention, medication and response information
outputs: verified care source set and unresolved documentation questions

steps.what: Document assessment results, interventions, medications, patient responses and treatment changes in the encounter record
inputs: verified care source set and unresolved documentation questions
outputs: draft care documentation with source references

steps.what: Verify care documentation against sources, correct discrepancies and approve the final record
inputs: draft care documentation with source references
verified care source set and unresolved documentation questions

tasks.design: Configure source-linked care documentation in the existing clinical record {OTHER}, reusing only existing authorised structured events. The nurse enters narrative observations and missing context manually and verifies that the final record distinguishes planned treatment, actual administration and patient response.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supported care events may be re-entered into several documentation sections.
tasks.enabler_now: Native record configuration can reuse authorised structured fields without inferring unrecorded care or generating a diagnosis.
tasks.still_hard: Preserve chronology, distinguish plans from completed care and document clinically meaningful responses.
tasks.human_edge: Identify an accurate-looking entry that misrepresents what happened.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated documentation with retained responsibility for care meaning.

reach.learn: Which repeated entries can safely reuse the same event

evidence.claim: Native reuse of authorised care events is an E1 configuration proposal; scribe case percentages do not measure this design.

assumptions: The observing nurse produces source findings during assessment, administering staff record actual medication events, and authorised clinicians record treatment changes during existing care; their unchanged capture is outside this documentation-only reuse baseline.
Reusable event contracts include patient and encounter identifier, event type, value or action, status, timestamp and author; plans are never treated as completed actions.
The nurse verifies sources in s1 and captures missing narrative in retained s2 time; no free structured patient-response code is assumed.
Configure existing record sections first; missing provenance or conflicting status requires manual entry and clarification.
Savings require genuine repeated entry and are zero where the record already reuses events. Acquisition and clinical assessment are excluded from both baseline and saving.
unknowns: Actual repeated-entry share and source event quality
research_questions: Can event reuse preserve chronology and completion status after all narrative capture and final review?

already_counted.description: Source identification and final record comparison remain fully counted.
Manual narrative and source-reuse review remain counted.

incremental.description: Nurse checks changed record sections and reports source-status mismatches.
Clinical documentation administrator maintains source field reuse and tests corrections.

approvals.approved_version: Exact corrected care documentation including patient, encounter, assessment, actual interventions, medication status, response, treatment changes and chronology; any source or text change voids approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B=100, R=25+22.5+30=77.5; gross 22.5 less 2 focal upkeep gives net 20.5. High requires repeated structured entry today; low covers existing reuse or manual clarification consuming gains. No clinical care time is saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Preserve acute assessment and patient discussion while reducing verified repeated care documentation.
reach: Clarify clinical uncertainty with responsible clinicians
Improve event reuse with documentation leads
role.ambitious_version: An acute care nurse with reliable source-linked records and preserved attention for changing patient conditions.
